claim: Let (S) be the following problem statement: every finite connected simple graph with maximum degree at most 2 is a path or a cycle. A path may have one vertex; a cycle has at least three vertices. If (S) holds, then every finite connected simple graph with at least three vertices and degree exactly 2 at every vertex is a cycle.

A path may have one vertex; a cycle has at least three vertices. If (S) holds, then every finite connected simple graph with at least three vertices and degree exactly 2 at every vertex is a cycle.
quadruple.stage: Finite simple graphs with adjacency, degree and connectedness, under the stated hypothesis (S)

shape.objects: Finite connected simple graphs, encoded in this fixture by a vertex list and a symmetric irreflexive adjacency table. The family has unbounded order n. This record defines its own encoding and supplies no Lean or Mathlib definition of it. The deduction does not construct objects from partial approximations or an amplifying operation.
shape.quantifiers: The claim is the entire implication (S) implies T. Hypothesis (S) quantifies over all finite connected simple graphs with maximum degree at most 2. Consequent T quantifies over all finite connected simple graphs with n >= 3 and all degrees exactly 2. A counterexample to T alone does not refute the implication: (S) must hold too. Relabelling onto {1,...,n} is equivalent to the abstract hypothesis, not a new mathematical assumption.
shape.target_quantity: A yes/no structural property: given (S), every connected 2-regular graph of order n >= 3 is a cycle. No numerical optimum or effective constant is sought. The threshold is explicitly n_0 = 3; a qualitative argument settles the claim.
shape.ambient_structure: Finite undirected simple graph incidence alone, without a second interacting kind of structure, probability space, gluing operation or transport family. Restricting the objects to paths and cycles gives a simpler class in which (S) holds. It is a subclass, not a second ambient carrying the original statement verbatim.
shape.symmetries: Vertex relabellings preserve adjacency, degrees, connectedness, paths and cycles. Every n-vertex graph is isomorphic to a graph on {1,...,n}, so that restriction of the hypothesis is equivalent. Removing a vertex can destroy 2-regularity and connectedness.
shape.configuration: Connectedness and degree exactly 2 at every vertex, expressed by adjacency. The required structural conclusion is that the graph is a cycle. Deletion can destroy these conditions. There is no forbidden subgraph avoidance or density target.
shape.extremal_candidate: Cycles C_n for n >= 3 are the proposed structural family and satisfy the consequent. Extremal here records a classification candidate, not a maximizer of a numerical quantity. No opposite-side numerical construction is used.
shape.finite_certificates: A cyclic ordering can certify the cycle property of one graph by checking all adjacencies. It does not certify the universal hypothesis (S) or the implication for unbounded n. There is no bounded computational residue or seed with positive excess.
shape.monotonicity: The family is indexed by n, but the structural implication is not a bound weakened by increasing a critical parameter. No monotone parameter or smallest open value is recorded.
shape.uniformity_parameter: Only graph order n varies. The same deduction works for every n >= 3, and no uniform quantitative estimate is missing.
shape.proof_shape: The explicit deduction in proof/adopted-cycle.md was drafted before this objective: fix a graph with n >= 3 and every degree equal to 2; apply (S) to obtain path or cycle; a path on n >= 3 vertices has endpoints of degree 1, so the graph is a cycle. The threshold is n_0 = 3. No theorem proving (S), numerical loss, solver computation or model-only substitution enters. The conditional theorem is the whole claim. A later closing move must name the adopted proof as its output; native proof acceptance and unit evidence are separate checks.
shape.neighbours: The stronger unconditional statement T and the classification statement (S) are elementary finite graph assertions. On the subclass of paths and cycles, (S) is true by definition. The labelled formulation on vertex sets {1,...,n} is equivalent by relabelling. No correspondence to a different setting, independent statement, model with a dropped kind of structure, or open countable case is recorded. Small graph instances are computable.
shape.known_bounds: For the implication, the fixture holds a complete direct deduction with threshold 3 in proof/adopted-cycle.md. There is no recorded equivalence of input (S) and target T, no failed quantitative method, first moment, numerical gap or finite computational residue. The unproved input for the conditional route is (S) inside this objective; the fixture makes no claim that (S), T or their implication is new or open research.
shape.missing_input: For T, the recorded classification route has exactly one input: the named problem statement (S). Within this objective (S) is assumed, not proved. For the implication itself nothing is missing: the adopted deduction supplies T from (S). Restriction to labelled graphs is equivalent to (S); restriction to 2-regular graphs is only the special case used by the proof.
shape.base_theory: Classical finite graph theory inside ZFC. Hypothesis (S) is a statement inside that theory, not an additional set-theoretic axiom or guessing principle. The finite encoding and any machine check of it stay inside the theory. No uncountable-cardinal difficulty or independence claim is involved.

known: Definitions: a path on n >= 2 vertices has endpoints of degree 1; a cycle on n >= 3 vertices is connected and 2-regular.
The fixture's direct deduction in proof/adopted-cycle.md proves the implication without proving (S). It is an elementary format example with no novelty claim.
